data.narrative:
Oxide Computer Company, a Series C semiconductor design firm founded by Steve Tuck and Bryan Cantrill, has raised $389M to date. The valuation assessment draws from a peer universe of 8 private and 3 public semiconductor companies, including same-stage comparables DEEPX ($529M, Series C) and Nearfield Instruments ($1.6B, Series D), as well as public anchors NVDA, AMD, and ALAB.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis, using the $389M raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yields $661M. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (Tenstorrent, Nearfield, Positron AI, and DEEPX) produces a $1.3B implied valuation, with the peer range spanning $529M to $2.7B. Public-comp anchoring via semiconductor P/S multiples (18.9x median) cannot be applied without disclosed revenue figures, which private companies typically do not disclose.

The two applicable methods triangulate to a low of $562M, median of $981M, and high of $1.5B. Key uncertainties include Oxide's revenue scale relative to peers, capital efficiency of the $389M deployed, and competitive positioning within a crowded frontier-semiconductor cohort. The wide peer range ($529M–$2.7B) underscores stage and execution variance; narrowing the valuation range would require visibility into customer traction and cash burn trajectory.
